title: Buyer Guide: Swapping the Homesite on a Homesite Reservation
content:
A Homesite Reservation may be moved from one homesite to another available homesite. The answers below state the swap terms; every figure named is that of the premium class shown.

**How many swaps are allowed, and what do they cost?**
A buyer may swap up to the class's maximum swaps per reservation. The first swaps, up to the class's number of free swaps, carry no fee; each later swap costs the swap fee of the class being left, collected before the swap is written.

**In which status can a reservation be swapped?**
A swap is allowed only on a reservation whose status is pending deposit or held, as shown on that reservation's record.

**By when must a swap be requested?**
A swap must be requested within the class's swap window days after the reservation date. Counting starts the day after the reservation date, and the last counted day is included.

**Can the reservation move to another community?**
Only where the class being left allows a swap into another community.

**What happens to the required funds?**
The new homesite's class sets the required funds from the swap date. Where they rise, the difference is due within the deposit due days of the new class. Where they fall and the class refunds the difference on a swap down, the difference is refunded with the refund reason swap down difference.

**Does a swap move the hold expiry date?**
The hold expiry date is not changed by a swap where the class does not restart the hold period on a swap.

## Swap window illustration (hypothetical window of 5 days, reservation date 1 May)

| Request date | Day count | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| 6 May | day 5, the last counted day | Yes |
| 7 May | day 6 | No |

## Fee illustration (hypothetical class allowing 1 free swap)

The first swap carries no fee; a second swap costs the swap fee of the class being left at the time of that second swap.
